articles.title: Anti-scam settings on iPhone, Pixel and Galaxy you should check
articles.summary: Apple's Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 27 can flag suspicious activity inside apps, but the setting is off by default and must be enabled.
articles.body: Scammers have become very good at getting us to do the dirty work for them. Someone may pose as your bank, claim your account was hacked or tell you to move money before something terrible happens. The call or message might sound convincing enough that you willingly follow the instructions. That's one reason a new iOS 27 setting caught my attention. Apple calls it Impersonation Risk Detection, and it can help supported apps recognize signs that you may be acting under the influence of a scammer. If you use Android, keep reading. Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy phones have their own built-in scam protections, and some of them go after the problem from a different direction. I would check these settings no matter which of these phones is in your pocket. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better healthcare. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com SCAMMERS ARE BUYING GOOGLE ADS TO STEAL BANK LOGINS What Impersonation Risk Detection does on iPhone Apple introduced Impersonation Risk Detection with iOS 27. The feature is designed to help with active social engineering scams, where someone pressures or guides you into doing something yourself. That last part is important. Traditional security can help block malware or stop an unauthorized login. However, those defenses can have a harder time helping when you are the legitimate account holder and a scammer has convinced you to send money or change sensitive account information. When you perform certain sensitive actions inside a supported third-party app, that app can ask Apple for a risk assessment. Apple says examples may include making a payment or changing critical security information such as a password. The app then receives one of three risk levels: From there, the app decides how to respond. It might ask you to verify your identity, delay an action or display a warning before letting you continue. That could give you one more opportunity to stop when a scammer is rushing you through a payment or account change. How Apple's anti-scam feature decides something looks suspicious Impersonation Risk Detection looks at signals related to how you are using your device. Apple says those signals can include interaction patterns, timing, context and basic sensor data. Apple's privacy documentation gives some additional examples. Your iPhone may consider whether you are sharing your screen as well as the approximate number of recent phone calls or emails you have received. It can combine that assessment with certain Apple Account information, including recent App Store downloads and purchases. The goal is to look for unusual behavior that could suggest someone is guiding or pressuring you. However, there is an important limitation. This feature works only with third-party apps that support Apple's Impersonation Risk Detection system. Turning it on does not give every app on your iPhone automatic scam detection. What Apple can see when you use Impersonation Risk Detection Apple says it never analyzes the content of your Photos, Messages or Mail for this feature. The underlying device information used to create the assessment also stays protected from both Apple and the requesting app. There is still some information sharing you should understand before turning it on. Your iPhone creates an on-device assessment and sends that assessment, rather than the underlying device data, to Apple. Apple can then combine it with certain Apple Account activity to generate the final risk signals. Apple also learns the category of activity you were attempting, such as signing in or making a payment. Apple says it does not learn which app requested the signals or the content of what you were doing inside the app. The requesting app receives the resulting risk level. It does not receive the underlying information Apple used to produce it. Why the iPhone anti-scam setting is off by default Apple requires you to choose whether supported apps can request Impersonation Risk Detection signals. As a result, Share with App Developers starts out turned off. That means simply updating your iPhone to iOS 27 does not activate the protection. You need to go into Settings and enable it yourself. One warning from Apple really stands out. If somebody on the phone tells you to disable Impersonation Risk Detection, Apple says you might be dealing with a scammer. I would treat a request like that as a major red flag. Hang up and contact the company using a number or app you already trust. How to turn on Impersonation Risk Detection in iOS 27 Here's how to check the setting on an iPhone running iOS 27: Apple says changes to this setting may take up to 24 hours to take effect. After you turn it on, you can return to Settings > Privacy & Security > Impersonation Risk Detection to see which apps have recently requested a risk assessment. You can also review why each app requested access and turn off access for individual apps. Samsung Galaxy phones have built-in scam and spam protection Samsung Galaxy phones also include tools designed to identify suspicious callers, although the exact features you see can vary by model, carrier and software version. On many Galaxy phones, Caller ID and spam protection is the main setting to check. Samsung uses technology from Hiya to identify suspected spam, scam and potential fraud calls, including numbers that aren't saved in your contacts. Samsung also offers a separate real-time Scam detection feature on some compatible Galaxy phones running One UI 8.5 or higher. Samsung says that feature can analyze calls for scam patterns and alert you with a tone or vibration. However, that option does not appear on every Galaxy phone, even when the device is running current software. Samsung began rolling out One UI 9 in September 2026, starting with the Galaxy S26 series after its debut on Samsung's newest foldables. Feature availability can still depend on your model, carrier and region. MAKE UNKNOWN CALLERS EXPLAIN WHY THEY'RE CALLING How to check scam and spam protection on Samsung Galaxy On a Samsung Galaxy, the exact options can vary by model, carrier and software version. To check the protection available on your phone: Samsung uses call-identification technology from Hiya to help identify suspected spam and scam callers, including numbers that aren't saved in your contacts. On compatible Galaxy phones, you may also see Call screening in the Phone app's settings. That feature can handle certain incoming calls before you answer. Samsung documents Call screening for compatible phones running One UI 8.5 or higher. Pixel owners have Scam Detection for calls Google takes a different approach on Pixel phones. Its Scam Detection feature can analyze a phone conversation in real time and warn you when the call shows patterns commonly associated with fraud. In the U.S., Google currently supports call Scam Detection on eligible Pixel 6 and later devices, with some model-specific exceptions. Pixel 9 and newer models use Gemini Nano on the device for scam detection during calls. Google says the feature works on the device. However, the company also warns that it cannot detect every scam, so a call that receives no warning should never automatically be considered safe. How to turn on call Scam Detection on Pixel To check it: Call Scam Detection requires you to opt in. If Google detects patterns associated with a scam during an eligible call, your Pixel can warn you while the conversation is still happening. That's useful because many scams become more convincing once a criminal gets you talking. The scammer can adjust the story based on what you say and keep applying pressure. Pixel can warn you about suspicious messages too Pixel owners have another protection worth checking. Scam Detection for chat messages can analyze new message notifications from supported apps and warn you when something looks suspicious. Google says this feature is available in the U.S. and several other countries. In the U.S., Scam Detection can also work with Gboard in select messaging apps and warn you as you begin responding to a suspicious message. Google expanded that capability with its September 2026 Pixel update. Unlike call Scam Detection, message Scam Detection is turned on by default. How to check message Scam Detection on Pixel Google says the feature runs in a secure, isolated environment. Your message content stays private and is not sent to Google unless you choose to share a message after receiving an alert. Google's September 2026 Pixel update is rolling out to supported Pixel devices running Android 17, so I would also make sure your Pixel has the latest available system update installed. SCAMMERS KNOW THE BEST TIME TO TEXT YOU Apple, Pixel and Galaxy approach scam detection differently These features aren't interchangeable, which is actually helpful. Apple's Impersonation Risk Detection focuses on signs that you may be getting manipulated while performing sensitive actions inside supported apps. Pixel can watch for scam patterns during calls and suspicious messages. Samsung can analyze supported calls for scam patterns. A scam may also move between several channels. Someone could text you first, get you on the phone and eventually convince you to open a legitimate banking app. Having protections at different points in that process gives your phone more opportunities to warn you before money or account information changes hands. What to do when your phone warns you about a possible scam Treat a scam warning as a reason to stop and verify what is happening. Don't keep following the caller's instructions while trying to decide whether the warning is right. Hang up if you're on a suspicious call. Then contact the bank, government agency or company directly using its official app, website or a phone number you already trust. The same goes for payment alerts. Open your financial institution's official app yourself and check the account. Don't use a phone number or link supplied by the person who contacted you. Also remember the reverse. No warning does not prove that a call, message or transaction is legitimate. Apple and Google both make clear that these systems can miss scams. Don't rely on your phone to catch every scam I like these features, but I would use them as another layer rather than my only protection. Scammers constantly change their scripts. They can spoof caller ID, impersonate companies you know and use personal information to make a fake story sound believable. If someone unexpectedly asks for a password, verification code or payment, slow down. A demand to transfer money to a "safe account" should also send up an immediate warning sign. Strong antivirus software can help protect against malicious links, phishing sites and malware that may appear alongside these scams. A password manager can also help by generating unique passwords and making it harder to reuse the same credentials across accounts. The phone can warn you. You still get the final say. For years, we've relied heavily on spam filters and caller warnings to keep criminals away. Now our phones are starting to look for what happens after the conversation begins. Apple's approach in iOS 27 could be especially useful when a scammer has already convinced you to open a legitimate app and take action yourself. Pixel can warn about suspicious calls and messages, while some compatible Galaxy phones can detect scam patterns during calls. articles.title: Tim Cook says ‘I’m not meddling’ in the new Apple CEO’s business
articles.summary: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO in September, but in an interview with The Independent, Cook says he’s “not meddling” in new CEO John Ternus’ work.
articles.body: Tim Cook stepped down as Apple CEO in September, handing over the top job to former hardware chief John Ternus and taking an executive chairman role. Cook’s still a visible representative of the company, having been recently photographed attending a state dinner at the White House. But in an interview with The Independent, Cook says he’s “not meddling” in Ternus’ work. “First of all, John and I have an incredible level of trust in each other,” Cook said. “The relationship must be based on trust, and the communication must be frequent and significant. But other than that, what I’m focused on right now is worldwide policy. And the interface with governments around the world matters because there are lots of things where we’re trying to advance or advocate for change. There’s a significant amount of work in that, and I’m doing that and helping John in any way he sees fit. I’m not meddling. I’m not a meddler.” Cook also said he’s told Ternus to “make it your own job. Put your time in the things that you can add the most value to around the company. And that means don’t mimic me. Just like I didn’t mimic Steve. We all have different strengths.” (Ternus told staff that, based on advice from Cook, “I need to spend my time where I can add the most value for Apple,” Bloomberg recently reported.) In the interview, Cook discussed how he wanted to make the leadership transition to Ternus “the best transition ever, a textbook example that people could look back to and learn from.” The transition “actually started years ago,” according to Cook, and he said that “I think everything has gone sort of exactly the way I had envisioned it.” Ternus introduced the iPhone Duo just days after taking over, and Cook said that he “wanted John to have some wind at his back.”

articles.title: Microsoft 365 Family subscribers will finally be able to share AI benefits
articles.summary: Microsoft is making lots of changes to its Microsoft 365 Family and Premium plans. Both will get shared AI benefits, but OneDrive storage is changing.
articles.body: Microsoft bundled its AI-powered Office features into Microsoft 365 Personal and Family subscriptions last year, but it only allowed the primary account holder to access the AI benefits. Now, Microsoft is about to let Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers share Copilot and AI usage features, alongside access to Office apps and OneDrive storage, with up to five other people on a plan. In an email to Microsoft 365 Family and Premium subscribers seen by The Verge, Microsoft outlines the changes that are coming to subscription plans over the coming months: * AI for everyone on your plan: Share your Copilot benefits and AI usage with other members on your plan. Plus, manage AI access for younger family members. * More flexible AI usage: Your individual AI feature limits will shift to a single AI usage allowance that you can apply to the advanced AI features you use most. Plus, purchase more AI usage when you need it. * More flexible cloud storage: Your cloud storage allowance will change from 1 TB per person to 2 TB of shared storage so everyone on the plan can use the free space while keeping their own accounts and files private. This change will apply after your first renewal after 2nd May, 2027. The storage changes seem like the major downside to Microsoft’s updates. Instead of getting 1TB of OneDrive storage per account, Microsoft is now limiting this to just 2TB of shared storage across the entire plan. Microsoft argues this makes storage more flexible if one member exceeds 1TB, but it looks like it’s an easy way for the company to upsell more OneDrive storage in reality. According to a support note, “Existing subscribers in eligible markets might also qualify for transitional bonus storage.” Microsoft is also planning to provide support to families that use a lot of storage The changes are being announced a year after Microsoft 365 Premium launched, which offers all the benefits of a Copilot Pro and a Microsoft 365 Family subscription for $19.99 a month. The “more flexible AI usage” change could mean that some subscribers end up paying more for AI usage, depending on how they’re using Copilot.

articles.title: Did You Know Bigg Boss Malayalam 8 Wildcard Contestant Vipin Was a Participant in The Next Top Anchor?

articles.body: One of the four wildcard entrants in Bigg Boss Malayalam 8, Vipin Das Nair is no stranger to reality television. The show was judged by a panel comprising Nyla Usha, Sabumon, Karthik Surya and Meenakshi. Vipin’s audition video is now gaining attention on social media following his entry into the Bigg Boss house. Besides acting, he was also passionate about anchoring, which prompted him to audition for the show.Vipin shared a video on his social media account announcing the good news after clearing the first round of Malayalam’s first anchoring reality show, The Next Top Anchor. However, when he arrived, he found hundreds of participants waiting there. He also pointed out that he was excited to audition in front of a judging panel featuring some of his favourite artists. He waited a while before sharing the news, until his episode was telecast.Vipin Nair also made a brief cameo in the Malayalam film Bharatanatyam, starring Saiju Kurup. He entered Bigg Boss Malayalam 8 as one of the four wildcard entrants, hoping to take the next step in his career.Since entering the house as a wildcard contestant, Vipin has been adopting a different strategy in the Bigg Boss house, keeping viewers on their toes. As he has limited Malayalam reading skills, his confession room sessions with Bigg Boss make for entertaining viewing. articles.title: How to save a video frame as a photo on your phone
articles.summary: iPhone, Samsung Galaxy and Google Pixel each hide a built-in tool that turns a video frame into a separate photo without any screenshot needed.
articles.body: Have you ever recorded a great video and then realized the moment you really wanted was buried somewhere in the middle? Maybe your grandchild flashed the perfect smile for half a second. Perhaps your dog made an expression you could never get again. You might even have caught the exact moment someone crossed a finish line or blew out birthday candles. A lot of us would pause the video and take a screenshot. That can work, but your phone may already have a better way to pull a frame directly from the video and save it as its own photo. Apple now makes this especially easy in iOS 27. Google Pixel and Samsung Galaxy owners can do it too, although the buttons are in different places. Here's how to find them. Join us for a free CyberGuy LIVE class. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson shares practical ways to stay safer, smarter and more confident with technology. Explore classes on stopping spam, phone security, financial protection and using AI to get better health care. Each class is free, easy to follow and comes with a free printable checklist. See the classes and register at CyberGuyLive.com. HOW TO SEARCH ANYTHING ON IPHONE, GALAXY AND PIXEL How to save a video frame as a photo on iPhone Apple added a dedicated Save Video Frame as Photo option to the Photos app in iOS 27. It lets you find a specific moment in a video and save that frame as a separate image in your photo library. Steps to save a video frame on iPhone Your iPhone saves the frame as a separate photo in the Photos app. To find the photo you just saved, open Photos, tap Collections at the bottom, scroll to Recent Days, then tap Saved Today and look for the new frame. How to save a video frame as a photo on Samsung Galaxy Samsung Galaxy phones have a similar tool built into the Gallery app. Once you find the moment you want, you can use the capture button to turn that video frame into a photo. Steps to capture a video frame on Samsung Galaxy Samsung notes that menus and settings can vary by Galaxy model, software version and region. To find the photo you just captured, open Gallery, tap Albums, tap View all if needed, then open the Video captures album. 12 BIGGEST APPLE WWDC 2026 TAKEAWAYS YOU NEED TO KNOW How to save a video frame as a photo on Google Pixel Pixel owners can use Google Photos to pull a still image from a video. Google calls the feature Export frame. Google has changed where this control appears in newer versions of Photos, so you may need an extra tap before you see it. Steps to export a video frame on Google Pixel Settings and wording may vary slightly depending on your version of Google Photos. If Export frame does not immediately appear, do not assume the feature disappeared. In newer versions of Google Photos, selecting the frame or tapping the camera icon can reveal the export control. Google Photos saves that moment as a separate still image. To find the photo you just created, return to the main Google Photos screen and look in your recent photos. You can also tap Collections and check the relevant album if needed. Why save a video frame instead of taking a screenshot? Taking a screenshot can still get the job done, especially when you are in a hurry. However, using the built-in frame tool gives you a dedicated photo created from the moment you selected in the video. It also makes the process easier because you do not have to worry about hiding video controls before taking the screenshot. Once the frame is saved, you can treat it like another photo in your library. The finished image can only be as good as the frame inside the original video. A sharp frame from a high-resolution video may look great. On the other hand, fast movement, low light or heavy compression can leave an individual frame blurry. ANDROID MALWARE CAN STEAL YOUR PIN AND BANK LOGINS Take your time before choosing the frame Here is one tip that can make a big difference. Slowly move through the video around the moment you want instead of stopping at the first frame that looks good. Just a fraction of a second can change someone's expression or give you a sharper image. You may also find a frame with less motion blur than the one you originally noticed. This is especially handy with family videos, pets and sporting events where the best moment can disappear almost instantly. Don't confuse this with Live Photos or Motion Photos There is another phone trick that sounds similar but works differently. An iPhone Live Photo captures a brief period of movement around a still photo. Many Android phones offer a similar feature called Motion Photo. With those, you can often go back and choose a better frame from the short clip surrounding the original picture. Here, we are starting with an actual video and pulling one frame from that recording to create a separate still image. If you are trying to rescue a group photo because somebody blinked, Live Photos and Motion Photos may be the better place to start. What if you can't find the photo afterward? Start with the same photo app you used to create the frame. On iPhone, the saved frame goes into your Photos library. On a Galaxy phone, Samsung saves it in Gallery and may also place it inside the Video captures album. Pixel owners will find the exported image in Google Photos. If you have thousands of photos on your phone, search can save you from endless scrolling. Names, locations and objects can often help narrow down the image much faster. Kurt's key takeaways I like this trick because so many of the moments we want to keep happen while we're recording video. You may think you missed the photo, only to discover that the exact expression or moment you wanted was sitting inside the recording all along. Apple, Google and Samsung each approach the feature a little differently, but you can get to the same result without downloading another app. Before deleting a video or giving up on a shot you thought you missed, take a closer look at the frames inside it. You may find a keeper. Have you ever pulled a great photo out of a video, and what other camera feature do you wish Apple, Google or Samsung would make easier to find? articles.title: The AI is in the computer
articles.summary: Amazon’s Alexa Tablets, Googlebooks, Apple’s HomePad, Microsoft’s Surface Ultra, and more on The Vergecast.
articles.body: It’s gadget season, and a lot of companies are launching a lot of new products. But whether it’s Microsoft dropping a high-end laptop, Amazon shipping a fancy Android tablet, or Apple diving headlong into the smart home, the actual strategy appears to be almost always the same. All these companies believe AI assistants and agents are the future of computing, and they’re building devices that put them front and center. On this episode of The Vergecast, David and Nilay dig into all this new hardware to figure out whether any of it has the right take on AI. articles.title: Microsoft tries to spark new life into Windows
articles.summary: Windows is slowly morphing into an agentic OS.
articles.body: When Microsoft released Windows 11 five years ago, it felt like an operating system that was still being renovated, a work in progress. You’d think by now that those renovations would be complete, with Microsoft turning its attention to Windows 12. Instead, Windows 11 feels like it’s here to stay, forming the foundation for Microsoft’s next big ambition: transforming Windows into an agentic OS. At a Windows and Surface event this week, Microsoft laid out its plan to bring AI agents to Windows, including hybrid intelligence that lets Windows take advantage of free local models instead of expensive cloud ones. “I think today is the day we’ll start talking and thinking about the frontier ecosystem taking maybe slightly different contours,” said Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella. After trying to sell businesses on a new Copilot last month, Nadella took a similar approach for his vision of agents and hybrid intelligence for Windows. It was so similar that when he mentioned the security, identity, and management aspects of Microsoft’s platform for securing agents, it almost seemed like he was pitching businesses again instead of AI developers, creatives, and just regular Windows users. After a somewhat dizzying start, Windows chief Pavan Davuluri appeared onstage to try and explain why agents and hybrid intelligence are so important for Windows users. There were demos of GitHub Copilot coding locally without expensive cloud tokens; a long list of models that can now run locally; examples of agents like OpenClaw, Hermes, and Perplexity; and even deeper integration of Copilot in Windows. I wasn’t fully convinced by any of these demos, though. I wanted to see what practical benefits local AI models could actually deliver for regular Windows users, instead of just the AI builders or developers Microsoft is trying to win over right now. Those are the people who could help turn its agentic OS vision into reality, though, and many of them are using a MacBook Pro instead of Windows. Microsoft’s answer to tempt them across to Windows? The Surface Laptop Ultra. The Surface Laptop Ultra is the home for Microsoft’s agentic OS push. Nvidia’s RTX Spark chips power the device, and there’s enough raw GPU power to get AI models exceeding 120 billion parameters running locally. “We built it for developers and creators that push the limit of performance and want portability with exceptional craft,” said Davuluri. The Surface Laptop Ultra is the flagship RTX Spark device, though there are also similar laptops from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, and MSI. Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599, and some RTX Spark PCs can run all the way up to an eye-watering $6,999. Much like the very top of the MacBook Pro line, you’d have to really need 128GB of unified memory to spend that kind of money. For many AI builders it might just be worth it, though, especially if you can save thousands in token costs. For the rest of us, Microsoft had very little to show. A new Windows Search interface looks like it could be one of the best additions to Windows 11 in years, though. Microsoft has totally redesigned search to make it not only more modern, but a heck of a lot faster than before. I’ve gotten to the point where I disable the Bing results in Windows Search, but this new UI now surfaces results in-line and lets you use search more like a launcher. I wasn’t expecting some grand unveiling of Windows 12 at this event, but I was hoping to hear a lot more about why RTX Spark laptops really do matter. “This is the future we’re building: agents that can work securely on your behalf, intelligence that moves seamlessly between local and cloud, and devices that become more capable than ever before,” said Davuluri. The problem is Microsoft is still in the early stages of this future it’s betting on for Windows. We had Copilot Plus PCs two years ago, with a big focus on the NPU chips inside that were supposed to revolutionize how consumers use everyday AI on a laptop. They haven’t done that yet, with only a handful of photo, video, and productivity tools making use of the NPU. Microsoft’s Recall feature was supposed to be the star of the NPU show, but the privacy concerns and delayed launch made it totally irrelevant instead. Nvidia’s presence and GPU dominance may well make RTX Spark a bigger success story than Copilot Plus PCs, but these machines are targeting a niche audience for now. If Microsoft and its partners want to move beyond selling them as MacBook Pro competitors, they’ll eventually need to bring the same capabilities to less expensive, less powerful devices and demonstrate practical reasons for regular Windows users to care. The difference is that RTX Spark PCs are aimed at people who have a much more immediate reason to care about local AI: developers and creators who need to run large models and can potentially save substantial amounts of money by doing so. For Microsoft, though, it’s the creators and builders that matter most right now. AI agents running in the cloud on Linux virtual machines could spark a wave of desktop Linux app compatibility we’ve never seen before. Microsoft needs to counter that threat by making Windows more agent-friendly. That might explain why Nadella and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang spent so much time reminiscing about the early days of the PC and graphics at this event. Microsoft isn’t ready to give up the PC dominance and app compatibility it has spent decades building. But it knows that the way people use computers is changing, and that Windows can’t rely on its historical advantages forever. Perhaps that gets to the heart of why Microsoft seems to be scrambling to embrace AI agents and hybrid intelligence in Windows. It needs to make sure that, even as computing shifts beyond the traditional PC, Windows remains at the center of it all.
